title: Export Working Capital Program: Eligibility and Underwriting
subtitle: Who qualifies for EWCP, what it can finance, the Ongoing Fee, and how lenders underwrite a self-liquidating export loan
sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B
learningObjectives: Apply EWCP eligibility rules, including operating history, reporting capability, EMC/ETC limits and NAICS exclusions
Distinguish eligible from prohibited EWCP uses of proceeds
Explain the EWCP Ongoing Fee payment options, invoicing schedule and consequences of non-payment
Compare transaction-specific, transaction-based and asset-based EWCP structures and the annual review gate
List the required elements of an EWCP credit analysis and how they differ from other 7(a) loans

topics.title: EWCP eligibility: who can borrow
topics.body:
The **Export Working Capital Program (EWCP)** (13 CFR 120.340-120.344) is SBA's short-term working capital guaranty for small business **Exporters engaged in Export Transactions**. Think of it as a trade-focused line of credit: it funds the gap between buying materials or making a product and getting paid by a foreign buyer.

As always, the lender starts with the Section A **Core Requirements**. EWCP then adds the following.

### Operating history

- The business must have **at least 12 full months of operations prior to filing an application**.
- If it does not, the Lender **may perform an analysis that demonstrates sufficient management experience** to move forward with the loan.

Compare this to Export Express, where the short-history exception needs both demonstrated export expertise and conventional underwriting. EWCP's exception is framed around a documented management experience analysis.

### Reporting capability

The Applicant must be able to produce **timely and accurate**:

- financial statements,
- accounts receivable and accounts payable agings, and
- inventory reports.

This is not a formality. EWCP is monitored through borrowing base reporting, so a borrower that cannot produce clean agings cannot be safely administered.

### Export management and trading companies

**Export management companies (EMCs)** and **export trading companies (ETCs)** may use EWCP **only if they take title** to the goods or services in the Export Transaction. An agent that just arranges sales on commission is not eligible. EMCs or ETCs with **any bank ownership are ineligible**.

### Excluded industries

| NAICS subsector | Industry | Export Express? | EWCP? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 721 | Accommodation | No | No |
| 457 | Gasoline Stations | No | No |
| 722 | Food Services and Drinking Places | (not listed) | **No** |

All three may be financed with **other SBA 7(a) assistance**.

> **Watch out:** EWCP adds NAICS 722 (restaurants and bars) to the exclusion list. A system that reuses the Export Express NAICS screen for EWCP will miss it.
keyPoints: EWCP is governed by 13 CFR 120.340-120.344.
Applicant needs at least 12 full months of operations before applying, or a Lender analysis showing sufficient management experience.
Applicant must produce timely, accurate financial statements, AR and AP agings and inventory reports.
EMCs and ETCs qualify only if they take title to the goods or services; any bank ownership makes them ineligible.
NAICS 721, 457 and 722 cannot use EWCP but may use other 7(a) assistance.
topics.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Eligibility for EWCP)

topics.title: EWCP: what proceeds can and cannot finance
keyPoints: Proceeds can finance only Export Transactions, single or multiple.
Eligible: export inventory, manufacturing costs, export goods/services, standby LCs, pre-shipment working capital, foreign AR financing, permitted fees.
Existing short-term export lines may be refinanced with collateral transfer per Appendix 14, Para. A.7.
Prohibited: domestic sales, fixed assets, floor plan on titled vehicles/equipment, overseas space.
No pre-shipment or purchase order financing under transaction-specific or transaction-based revolving facilities for Foreign-to-Foreign Export Transactions.
topics.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Eligible Uses of Proceeds for EWCP)

topics.title: EWCP loan size, guaranty, maturity and rate
topics.body:
### Loan amount

- The **maximum EWCP loan amount is $5,000,000**.
- Affiliation applies (13 CFR 120.151): the Lender must determine whether the Applicant has affiliates and **document the results in its credit analysis**. If affiliation exists, the maximum applies to the Applicant and all affiliates **as if they were a single business**.

### Where the other terms live

Unlike Export Express, the EWCP section of Chapter 5 does not restate the guaranty percentages or rate grid. It points to the appendices:

| Term | Reference |
|---|---|
| Debt refinancing | Appendix 14, Para. B.7 (and Para. A.7 for refinancing short-term export lines with collateral transfer) |
| Maximum guaranty amounts and percentages | Appendix 16, Para. B.6 |
| Loan maturities | Appendix 17, Para. B.7 |
| Interest rates | Appendix 18, Para. B.7.a |
| Collateral | Appendix 19, Para. B.7 |
| Personal guaranties | Section A, Ch. 5, Para. A |
| Fees lenders may charge | Section A, Ch. 4 |
| Guaranty application submission | Appendix 20 |
| Closing and disbursement (general) | Section B, Ch. 6, Para. D |

### Maturity in practice

The fee section of the chapter gives a useful fact about maturity: **the vast majority of EWCP loans have a maturity of 12 months or less, but EWCP loans may have a maturity of up to 36 months**. Asset-based EWCP lines are typically committed for 12 months and then renewed or re-issued annually.

> **In practice:** Because EWCP is short-term, the same borrower may come back every year. Each renewal triggers the annual credit review described later in this chapter, so build the renewal workflow around it.

> **Watch out:** Do not apply the Export Express interest rate chart to EWCP. EWCP rates are governed by Appendix 18, Para. B.7.a.
keyPoints: Maximum EWCP loan: $5,000,000, with affiliates counted as one business.
Guaranty amounts and percentages: Appendix 16, Para. B.6.
Maturities: Appendix 17, Para. B.7. Most EWCP loans mature in 12 months or less; maturity may be up to 36 months.
Interest rates: Appendix 18, Para. B.7.a.
Collateral: Appendix 19, Para. B.7; guaranties: Section A, Ch. 5, Para. A.
topics.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Loan Terms and Conditions for EWCP)

topics.title: The EWCP Ongoing Fee: monthly or annual payment
topics.body:
Every 7(a) loan carries an ongoing guaranty fee. EWCP has its own version, the **EWCP Ongoing Fee**, and lenders have a choice about how to pay it.

### The two options

For **EWCP loans approved after September 27, 2010**, the Lender may choose:

| | Option 1: Monthly | Option 2: Annual |
|---|---|---|
| How paid | With other 7(a) ongoing servicing fees to the **Fiscal Transfer Agent (FTA)**, along with the SBA Form 1502 | Per-loan annual invoice from SBA's **Denver Finance Center (DFC)** |
| Why choose it | EWCP may be a small part of the 7(a) portfolio; paying it with everything else is simple | Lender prefers to be billed |
| Total fee | Same | Same |

Either way, **the Lender must still submit SBA Form 1502 monthly on every 7(a) loan in its portfolio, including all EWCP loans**. Under Option 2, DFC uses the EWCP balances reported on the 1502s to compute the annual bill.

### Invoice timing under Option 2

| EWCP maturity | Invoices received |
|---|---|
| 12 months or less | One invoice, after maturity |
| More than 12, not more than 24 months | 12 months after closing, and after maturity |
| More than 24 months (up to 36) | 12 months after closing, 24 months after closing, and after maturity |

- DFC **mails the invoice within 60 days of each 12-month interval**.
- **Payment is due within 30 days of the invoice date**.
- The invoice covers the previous 12 months (or a shorter period if the loan matured early).
- Payment is made through **Pay.gov**.

### Monitoring

- The **FTA sends monthly EWCP reports** to DFC and SBA's **Office of International Trade (OIT)** tracking, by Lender: whether 1502s are being filed on EWCP loans, when annual invoices are due, and the accrued fee to be billed per loan.
- **DFC sends a monthly report** to OIT and the **Office of Credit Risk Management** listing lenders delinquent on invoiced EWCP fees.
- **OIT**, through delegation to the **Export Finance Manager**, monitors lenders' 1502 submissions and fee payments.

> **Watch out:** A Lender's failure to pay any fees (plus any resulting interest and penalties) may lead SBA to **suspend or revoke the Lender's eligibility to participate in the 7(a) program or to limit its delegated authority**. A missed EWCP invoice is a program-level risk, not just a billing issue.
keyPoints: For EWCP loans approved after September 27, 2010, Lenders choose monthly (Option 1) or annual (Option 2) payment of the EWCP Ongoing Fee.
Both options produce the same total fee.
SBA Form 1502 must be submitted monthly on all 7(a) loans, including EWCP, regardless of option.
Under Option 2, DFC mails an invoice within 60 days of each 12-month interval; payment is due within 30 days via Pay.gov.
Unpaid fees can lead SBA to suspend or revoke 7(a) eligibility or limit delegated authority.
topics.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Payment Options for EWCP Ongoing Guaranty Fee)

topics.title: EWCP credit standard and the three loan structures
topics.body:
### A different primary source of repayment

Most 7(a) loans are repaid from business cash flow. EWCP is different. SBA's credit standards still start with **13 CFR 120.101 and 120.150** and require a commercially reasonable, prudent analysis, but:

- EWCP loans are **self-liquidating**. The **conversion of export-related trading assets to cash** (inventory becomes a shipment, the shipment becomes a foreign receivable, the receivable is collected) is the **primary source of repayment**.
- If the analysis shows the Applicant **lacks reasonable assurance of timely repayment from the conversion of foreign sales into cash, the loan must be declined**, regardless of collateral or outside repayment sources.

### Three structures

When submitting, the Lender must specify which of these it is requesting:

| Structure | How it works | Field exam? |
|---|---|---|
| **Single transaction-specific loan** | Finances one identified export order or contract | Not required (transaction reviewed individually) |
| **Transaction-Based line of credit** | Supports single or multiple transactions during the loan term; may be **revolving or non-revolving** | Not required |
| **Asset-Based Loan (ABL)** | **Revolving** line supported by a **monthly Borrowing Base Certificate (BBC)** reporting levels of assets, typically receivables and inventory; **typically committed for 12 months** then renewed or re-issued annually | Required pre-disbursement at $1,000,000 or more |

### Annual and renewal credit reviews

For both Transaction-Based and Asset-Based EWCP loans, **on no less than an annual basis, and as part of any renewal**, the Lender must:

1. Obtain **updated year-end and interim financial statements**; and
2. Perform a **full review of the credit and collateral**.

The analysis must document that the Applicant:

- **Is creditworthy**;
- Has **reasonable assurance of timely repayment from the conversion of sales into cash**; and
- **Is in compliance with EWCP program requirements**.

If the analysis does not document **all three**, **no further disbursements may be made, and the loan may not be renewed** until the Applicant can demonstrate it meets them.

> **In practice:** Treat the annual review as a gate, not paperwork. A system should block draws on an EWCP line once the annual review date passes without a completed, passing review.
keyPoints: EWCP loans are self-liquidating: conversion of export trading assets to cash is the primary repayment source.
Decline if there is no reasonable assurance of timely repayment from converting foreign sales into cash, regardless of collateral.
Transaction-Based: a line supporting single or multiple transactions, revolving or non-revolving.
Asset-Based (ABL): revolving line supported by a monthly Borrowing Base Certificate, typically committed for 12 months.
At least annually, a full credit and collateral review must show creditworthiness, repayment from sales conversion, and program compliance; otherwise no further disbursements or renewal.
topics.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Credit Standards for EWCP), Specific Types of EWCP loans

topics.title: EWCP processing methods and the underwriting memo
topics.body:
### Two ways to process

| | Non-delegated | Delegated (PLP-EWCP) |
|---|---|---|
| Who decides | **SBA** makes the final determination on eligibility and creditworthiness | The **Lender**, under its PLP-EWCP authority |
| What SBA reviews up front | Uses of proceeds, adequacy of collateral, loan structure, any required equity injection | Nothing on credit or structure before issuing a loan number |
| When SBA reviews the analysis | During processing | When the Lender **requests purchase** of the guaranty or during **lender oversight** |

Note that EWCP has its own delegated authority, **PLP-EWCP**. Export Express, by contrast, is only processed under delegated Export Express authority, with no non-delegated path.

Under delegated processing, the Lender must still analyze creditworthiness under SBA Loan Program Requirements and **properly document its file**. The PLP-EWCP Lender's analysis is subject to SBA's **review and determination of adequacy** later.

### What the underwriting must do

- The Lender **must submit a credit memorandum with the application**.
- The analysis must be commercially reasonable and consistent with prudent lending standards, recognizing that EWCP loans are self-liquidating.
- The financial analysis should pay **particular attention to the Applicant's foreign payment terms and their impact on the Applicant's cash cycle**. Sixty-day terms to a buyer in one country and 180-day insured open account terms in another produce very different funding needs.
- The Lender must **specify whether the request is** for a single transaction-specific loan, a transaction-based revolving line of credit (single or multiple transactions), or an asset-based loan.

> **In practice:** The cash cycle drives line sizing. Map how many days pass from paying the supplier to collecting from the foreign buyer, multiply by daily export cost, and compare that to the requested line. The credit memo should show this math.

The detailed content of the credit analysis follows in the next two topics.
keyPoints: Non-delegated: SBA makes the final eligibility and credit decision, including uses, collateral, structure and equity.
Delegated: under PLP-EWCP authority SBA does not review credit or structure before issuing a loan number.
PLP-EWCP analysis is reviewed at guaranty purchase or during lender oversight.
A credit memorandum must accompany the application.
Pay particular attention to foreign payment terms and their impact on the cash cycle.
topics.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Credit Standards for EWCP), Processing Methods and Underwriting

topics.title: EWCP credit analysis, part 1: business, exports and financing
topics.body:
The EWCP credit analysis has a long required list. The first group of items explains **who the borrower is and why it needs this loan**.

### 1. Use of proceeds and benefit of the guaranty

An explanation of the use of proceeds and the benefits of the loan guaranty, including **details of the underlying transaction(s)** and **the countries where the buyers are located**.

### 2. Credit not available elsewhere

The factors showing the Applicant does **not have credit available elsewhere on reasonable commercial terms** from non-Federal, non-State, non-local government sources, per **Section A, Ch. 1, Para. H**.

### 3. The business and its management

The nature of the business, **length of time in business under current management**, and if applicable, **depth of management experience** in the industry or a related industry, with a brief description of the management team.

### 4. Export experience and export business plan

This may include:

- **Dollar amount of export revenue** (current or expected) and its **percentage of total revenue**;
- **Principal or proposed export markets**;
- **Proposed or established export customer relationships**;
- **Largest export sales contract to date**;
- **Export contract backlog**; and
- Documentation of the Applicant's **performance history on standby letters of credit**, which serve as bid, advance payment, performance, supplier and warranty guarantees or bonds.

### 5. Financing relationships

A summary of all short- and long-term debt relationships, such as:

- **Domestic revolving lines** or other term facilities, with purpose, payment structure and collateral;
- **Standby debt**: whether it permits interest payments, how much and how often, and under what conditions payments can be halted; and
- Any **SBA or other government-guaranteed financing**.

> **In practice:** The domestic line is a frequent friction point. The EWCP lender needs a clear picture of who holds liens on which receivables and inventory, because the EWCP borrowing base must be cleanly separated from the domestic lender's collateral.

### Credit history and franchise checks

The analysis must also include:

- A discussion of the **Lender's credit experience with the Applicant** and a review of **business and personal credit reports**; and
- For a **franchise (as defined by the FTC)**, review of franchisor credit information such as **failed franchisees and cash flow projections**, and review of any **management agreement** to determine whether it creates an **ineligible passive company** (unless it is part of the franchise disclosure documents for a brand on the Franchise Directory).
keyPoints: Explain use of proceeds and benefits of the guaranty, including the underlying transactions and buyer countries.
Show credit is not available elsewhere on reasonable commercial terms (Section A, Ch. 1, Para. H).
Describe the business, time under current management and management depth.
Discuss export experience and plan: export revenue, markets, customers, largest contract, backlog, standby LC performance.
Summarize all short- and long-term debt, standby debt terms, and any SBA or government-guaranteed financing.
topics.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Credit Standards for EWCP - Credit Analysis), Items 1-5 and 14-15

topics.title: EWCP credit analysis, part 2: financials, ratios and collateral
topics.body:
### 6. Historical and projected financial analysis

A financial analysis of the **two most recent years** of historical financial information (tax returns, or balance sheet with debt schedule and income statement) **plus an interim statement**. The Lender should also analyze **projections for at least 12 months after the first disbursement**. It must include:

- Historical cash flow and total debt service for the existing business;
- **Operating cash flow (OCF), defined as EBITDA**; and
- Documented additions and subtractions to cash flow, such as unfunded capital expenditures, non-recurring income, expenses and distributions, S-Corp tax distributions, rent payments, owner's draw, and a **global cash flow analysis** of significant affiliates.

### 7-8. Debt service and projections

- **Debt service (DS)** means future required principal and/or interest payments on **all business debt, including the new SBA loan**.
- For projections, the Lender should calculate debt service coverage and analyze the assumptions, such as reasons for a reduced expense structure, reasons for revenue growth (new product lines, sales channels, production facilities) and industry analysis.

### 9. Cash cycle repayment analysis

A financial analysis of **EWCP repayment ability based on the Applicant's cash cycle**. This is the heart of a self-liquidating loan.

### 10-11. Field examinations and ABL collateral

- Field examination rules apply to Asset-Based EWCP loans (covered in detail in the next chapter): a field exam is required **before first disbursement on Asset-Based EWCP loans of $1,000,000 or greater**, and **at least annually at $2,000,000 or greater**.
- For Asset-Based loans, a financial analysis of the collateral that **addresses any findings from the field examination**.

### 12. Ratios

| Required ratio benchmarks |
|---|
| Current Ratio |
| Debt / Tangible Net Worth |
| Debt Service Coverage |
| Inventory turnover |
| Receivables turnover |
| Payables turnover |

Plus any others the Lender considers significant for the industry.

### 13. Collateral analysis

This may discuss:

- **Buyer and export destination market risk**: economic, political, compliance, currency or logistics;
- **Anticipated terms of sale**: cash before or at shipment, irrevocable letters of credit, export credit insurance (comprehensive commercial and political risk), collections (cash against documents), open account, and for insured sales the credit coverage, allowed sales terms and the borrower's experience administering the policy; and
- **Composition and quality of the borrowing base**: quality of the customer base, **concentration risk**, delinquency volumes and trends, and **dilution**.

> **Watch out:** EWCP asks for **two** years of historical financials. The International Trade loan asks for **three**. Do not mix them up in a shared underwriting template.
keyPoints: Analyze two most recent years of historical financials plus an interim statement, and projections for at least 12 months after first disbursement.
Operating cash flow (OCF) is defined as EBITDA; debt service includes the new SBA loan.
Analyze repayment ability based on the Applicant's cash cycle.
Ratios: Current Ratio, Debt/Tangible Net Worth, Debt Service Coverage, inventory, receivables and payables turnover.
Collateral analysis covers buyer and country risk, terms of sale and borrowing base quality.
topics.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Credit Standards for EWCP - Credit Analysis), Items 6-13

topics.title: Fees on EWCP loans
topics.body:
Lender fees on SBA loans are tightly controlled. The baseline rules for **ethics, fees and Agents** are in **Section A, Ch. 4**, including the list of fees and expenses a Lender may collect from an Applicant or Borrower (Section A, Ch. 4, Para. C.2).

EWCP adds one important allowance.

### Extraordinary servicing fees on borrowing base loans

At the **time of the annual review**, a Lender **may charge extraordinary servicing fees in excess of 2%** for EWCP loans **that are disbursed based on a Borrowing Base Certificate**.

Why the allowance? Asset-based EWCP lines take real work to administer: monthly or quarterly BBCs, agings, inventory listings, control accounts, and field examinations. The allowance lets lenders recover the cost of that monitoring.

The guardrails:

- The fees must be **reasonable and prudent based on the level of extraordinary effort required**; and
- They **must not be higher than the fees charged on the Lender's similarly-sized, non-SBA guaranteed commercial loans**.

| Situation | Can the lender charge an extraordinary servicing fee above 2%? |
|---|---|
| Asset-based EWCP line disbursed against monthly BBCs, at annual review | Yes, if reasonable and no higher than on comparable conventional loans |
| Single transaction-specific EWCP loan not disbursed against a BBC | No, the allowance applies to BBC-disbursed loans |
| Fee higher than what the lender charges on its own similar conventional ABL lines | No |

> **Watch out:** The allowance applies "at the time of the annual review." It is not a license to charge monthly monitoring fees above the Section A limits throughout the year.

### Packaging fees and lender charges as eligible uses

Recall from the uses of proceeds list that EWCP proceeds may pay **lender fees and charges and any packaging fees** as permitted in the chapter. Fees not permitted by Section A, Ch. 4 or this allowance cannot be financed with EWCP proceeds.

### Submission

The guaranty application is submitted under **Appendix 20, Submission of Application for Guaranty**.
keyPoints: General fee, ethics and Agent rules are in Section A, Ch. 4.
At annual review, Lenders may charge extraordinary servicing fees in excess of 2% on EWCP loans disbursed against a Borrowing Base Certificate.
Such fees must be reasonable and prudent for the extra effort required.
They may not exceed fees charged on the Lender's similarly-sized non-SBA commercial loans.
topics.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Fees that the Lender May Charge the Borrower)

keyTerms.definition: SBA 7(a) program (13 CFR 120.340-120.344) guaranteeing short-term, self-liquidating working capital loans to small business Exporters, up to $5,000,000.
A loan repaid primarily by converting the financed export-related trading assets (inventory and foreign receivables) into cash.
An EWCP line of credit supporting single or multiple export transactions during its term, on a revolving or non-revolving basis.
A revolving EWCP line supported by a Borrowing Base Certificate reporting receivables and inventory, typically committed for 12 months and renewed annually.
A periodic borrower report of eligible collateral (typically foreign receivables and export inventory) used to determine how much may be advanced.
Delegated authority allowing a Lender to approve EWCP loans without SBA reviewing the credit or structure before a loan number is issued.
The ongoing guaranty fee on EWCP loans, payable monthly with Form 1502 (Option 1) or annually on DFC invoice (Option 2).
The monthly lender report on all 7(a) loans, including EWCP, submitted to the Fiscal Transfer Agent.
SBA office that invoices annual EWCP Ongoing Fees and reports delinquent lenders.
SBA office that, through Export Finance Managers, monitors EWCP fee payments and Form 1502 reporting.
Export management company / export trading company; eligible for EWCP only if it takes title to the goods or services and has no bank ownership.
For EWCP and IT credit analysis, earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA).
A defined export transaction type for which EWCP may not provide pre-shipment or purchase order financing under transaction-specific or transaction-based revolving facilities.

quiz.question: What is the maximum EWCP loan amount?
quiz.explanation: The maximum EWCP loan is $5,000,000, with affiliates counted as one business. $500,000 is the Export Express maximum and $2,000,000 is the IT working capital cap and a field exam threshold.
quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Loan Terms and Conditions for EWCP), Maximum Loan Amount

quiz.question: Which of these businesses is excluded from EWCP but could use Export Express?
options: A restaurant group (NAICS 722) that exports sauces
A hotel (NAICS 721)
A gas station (NAICS 457)
A machine shop (NAICS 332)
quiz.explanation: EWCP excludes NAICS 721, 457 and 722. Export Express excludes only 721 and 457. So a NAICS 722 business is barred from EWCP but not listed as excluded from Export Express. Hotels and gas stations are excluded from both; the machine shop is excluded from neither.
quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Eligibility for EWCP), Ineligible NAICS Codes

quiz.question: An export management company wants an EWCP line. Under which condition is it eligible?
options: It earns commissions on sales it arranges and has a minority bank shareholder
It takes title to the goods in the Export Transaction and has no bank ownership
It takes title to the goods and a bank owns 10% of it
It acts as agent only, without taking title, for multiple manufacturers
quiz.explanation: EMCs and ETCs may use EWCP only if they take title to the goods or services, and any bank ownership makes them ineligible. Commission-only agents and companies with bank ownership both fail.
quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Eligibility for EWCP), Para. 3

quiz.question: Which of the following is a prohibited use of EWCP proceeds?
options: Paying direct labor to manufacture goods for export
Supporting a performance standby letter of credit for an export contract
Post-shipment foreign accounts receivable financing
Buying a forklift for the borrower's warehouse
quiz.explanation: EWCP proceeds may not acquire fixed assets or capital goods for the borrower's business (13 CFR 120.342). Direct labor for export goods, export-related standby LCs and post-shipment foreign AR financing are all listed eligible uses.
quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Eligible Uses of Proceeds for EWCP)

quiz.question: What is the primary source of repayment for an EWCP loan?
options: Liquidation of the borrower's real estate collateral
Personal guaranties of the owners
Conversion of export-related trading assets to cash
Long-term business cash flow over a 10-year amortization
quiz.explanation: EWCP loans are self-liquidating; the conversion of export-related trading assets to cash is the primary source of repayment. If the analysis lacks reasonable assurance of repayment from converting foreign sales to cash, the loan must be declined regardless of collateral.
quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Credit Standards for EWCP)

quiz.question: At the annual review of an asset-based EWCP line, the lender documents that the borrower is creditworthy and compliant with program requirements, but cannot show reasonable assurance of repayment from converting sales into cash. What follows?
options: The line may be renewed if collateral coverage is strong
No further disbursements may be made and the loan may not be renewed until all three requirements are met
The lender may continue advances for 90 days while the borrower cures
The lender must immediately request SBA purchase
quiz.explanation: All three findings (creditworthy, reasonable assurance of repayment from conversion of sales into cash, program compliance) must be documented. If any is missing, no further disbursements and no renewal until the borrower can demonstrate all three. Strong collateral does not substitute, and there is no 90-day grace period.
quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Credit Standards for EWCP), Specific Types of EWCP loans, Annual and Renewal Credit Reviews

quiz.question: Under EWCP Ongoing Fee Option 2, when is payment due after DFC sends an invoice?
options: Within 30 days of the invoice date
Within 60 days of the invoice date
With the next monthly SBA Form 1502
At loan maturity
quiz.explanation: DFC mails the invoice within 60 days of each 12-month interval, and payment is due within 30 days of the invoice date via Pay.gov. The 60 days is the mailing window, not the payment window.
quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Payment Options for EWCP Ongoing Guaranty Fee)

quiz.question: A lender elects annual payment (Option 2) of the EWCP Ongoing Fee on an EWCP loan with a 30-month maturity. How many invoices will it receive and when?
options: One, after maturity
Two: 12 months after closing and after maturity
Three: 12 months after closing, 24 months after closing, and after maturity
Thirty monthly invoices
quiz.explanation: For maturities greater than 24 months, invoices come 12 months after closing, 24 months after closing, and after maturity. One invoice applies to 12 months or less; two invoices apply to more than 12 and not more than 24 months.
quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Payment Options for EWCP Ongoing Guaranty Fee)

quiz.question: A lender chose Option 2 (annual invoicing) for its EWCP fees. Which reporting obligation still applies?
options: None for EWCP loans; DFC tracks balances directly
Quarterly Form 1502 for EWCP loans only
Annual Form 1502 for EWCP loans with the fee payment
Monthly SBA Form 1502 reporting on all 7(a) loans, including EWCP
quiz.explanation: Regardless of payment option, the Lender must submit SBA Form 1502 monthly on all 7(a) loans, including EWCP. DFC computes the annual fee from those monthly-reported balances.
quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Payment Options for EWCP Ongoing Guaranty Fee)

quiz.question: A PLP-EWCP lender approves an EWCP line under its delegated authority. When does SBA review the adequacy of the lender's credit analysis?
options: Before issuing the loan number
When the Lender requests guaranty purchase or during lender oversight
Only if the loan exceeds $1,000,000
At each borrowing base certificate submission
quiz.explanation: Under PLP-EWCP authority SBA does not review credit or structure before issuing a loan number; the analysis is subject to SBA review at purchase or during oversight. Pre-approval review is the non-delegated method.
quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Credit Standards for EWCP), Processing Methods

quiz.question: How many years of historical financial information must an EWCP credit analysis cover?
options: The two most recent years plus an interim statement
The three most recent years plus an interim statement
One year plus 24 months of projections
Five years of tax returns
quiz.explanation: EWCP requires analysis of the two most recent years of historical financial information plus an interim statement, along with projections for at least 12 months after first disbursement. Three years is the International Trade requirement.
quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Credit Standards for EWCP - Credit Analysis), Item 6

quiz.question: At the annual review of an EWCP line disbursed against monthly BBCs, the lender wants to charge a 2.5% extraordinary servicing fee. Its fee on similar conventional ABL lines is 2.0%. Is the fee permitted?
options: Yes, any fee above 2% is allowed at annual review
Yes, because EWCP loans are not subject to Section A fee limits
No, extraordinary servicing fees are never allowed on EWCP
No, the fee may not exceed what the lender charges on similarly-sized non-SBA loans
quiz.explanation: Extraordinary servicing fees above 2% are allowed at annual review on BBC-disbursed EWCP loans, but they must be reasonable and no higher than on the lender's similarly-sized non-SBA commercial loans. 2.5% exceeds the 2.0% conventional fee.
quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Fees that the Lender May Charge the Borrower)

quiz.question: An applicant has been operating for 9 months. What does the SOP allow for EWCP?
options: Nothing; the business must wait until 12 full months
The Lender may perform an analysis demonstrating sufficient management experience to proceed
Eligibility only if export sales exceed 70% of revenue
Eligibility only under non-delegated processing
quiz.explanation: EWCP requires 12 full months of operations, but if the applicant lacks that history the Lender may perform an analysis demonstrating sufficient management experience to move forward. There is no export-percentage or processing-method condition.
quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Ch. 5, Para. B (Eligibility for EWCP), Para. 1
